content.title: About
content.content: Pork, chop, center cut, raw (code 5845) is a boneless piece taken from the central portion of a pork loin chop. The meat is light pink, tender and moderately marbled. It is commonly used for pan‑frying, baking or grilling and provides a good source of protein, B‑vitamins and minerals.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The center cut of a pork chop is considered the most tender and juicy part of the loin.
Pork contains all essential amino acids required by humans.
In traditional cuisines pork chops are often breaded or served with rich sauces.
Pork is a natural source of creatine, which supports muscle energy metabolism.
Raw pork chops are frequently marinated in acidic solutions (lemon, vinegar) to tenderize the fibers.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: Pork provides complete protein that is essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: It is rich in thiamine (B1), riboflavin (B2), niacin (B3) and vitamin B12, which support energy metabolism and nervous system health.

items.title: Minerals: iron and zinc
items.content: Iron aids oxygen transport, while zinc supports immune function and wound healing.

items.title: Creatine
items.content: Creatine can improve physical performance and help build lean muscle mass.

items.title: Selenium
items.content: Selenium acts as an antioxidant and supports thyroid function.

items.title: Bacterial contamination risk
items.content: Raw pork may harbor Salmonella, Campylobacter or Trichinella; it should be cooked to an internal temperature of 71 °C.

items.title: High saturated fat content
items.content: The cut can contain notable amounts of saturated fat, so people with high cholesterol should consume it in moderation.

items.title: Meat allergy
items.content: Rarely, some individuals may experience an allergic reaction to pork.

items.title: Digestive discomfort
items.content: Large portions can cause heaviness, especially in those with sensitive digestion.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Center‑cut pork chops can be pan‑seared, baked, grilled or braised. Marinating beforehand in olive oil, garlic, herbs and an acidic component (lemon juice or vinegar) helps tenderize the meat. Serve with vegetable sides, sauces, or sliced for salads.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep raw chops in a sealed container at 0–2 °C for 2‑3 days. For longer storage freeze at –18 °C in airtight packaging; thaw in the refrigerator. Discard any meat with off‑odors or discoloration.
